data.title: Hyperliquid Strategies’ HYPE Treasury Is About 1% From a Loss
data.description: Hyperliquid Strategies, the largest Hyperliquid treasury, would fall below its blended cost basis after an additional drop of about 1% in HYPE. The token fell about 28% over the past month and stood at $56.94 at press time, according to BeInCrypto, citing BeInCrypto Markets data. The company holds about 38.9 million HYPE, and its blended cost was $56.35 per token as of October 28, including staking rewards. Tokens it purchased had an average cost of $61.13 and are already underwater. During the September quarter, the company spent $785 million on 9.1 million HYPE, or roughly $86 per token, as the token traded near its record high. Its latest quarterly profit came mostly from paper gains on HYPE; if prices remain around current levels, its next report would likely show a large loss. Smaller rival Hyperion DeFi reported an average cost of $40 per token as of September 30.

data.title: Klingbeil Says Brunnermeier to Start as ECB Chief Economist in June
data.description: Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said Germany’s nominee Markus Brunnermeier would begin as European Central Bank chief economist in June, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Banca Monte dei Paschi Says Intesa Sanpaolo Bid Is Fair but Falls Short on Value
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena SpA said Intesa Sanpaolo SpA’s acquisition bid is fair financially but does not fully reflect the Tuscan lender’s value, days before shareholders begin deciding on the offer.

data.title: Darkfost: Bitcoin Capital Held at Unrealized Loss Hits Record High
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, crypto analyst Darkfost said the amount of capital invested in Bitcoin and currently at an unrealized loss has reached a record high. With Bitcoin trading near $58,000 and its market capitalization at about $1.17 trillion, roughly $950 billion in invested capital is at a loss, while about $119 billion is in profit. Darkfost noted that the figures measure invested capital, not the number of Bitcoin held at a loss, and reflect the financial pressure on underwater positions and the scale of investors’ losses.

data.title: STOCKS | Nvidia Plunges 14% in One Day as Dan Bin Says Some Funds Must Cut Holdings at Liquidation Threshold
data.description: U.S. stocks closed lower across the board, with the Nasdaq Composite down 5.28%, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index falling nearly 11%, and Nvidia plunging 14.01% in one session. According to Odaily, Dan Bin wrote on November 21 that he had “woken up to a bloodbath” and told investors that some funds reaching their liquidation threshold could only reduce holdings passively, while he maintained his view that artificial intelligence is in a decade-long bull market. Recent data show that Gao Yi Asset had exited Nvidia, Duan Yongping had cut his Nvidia position by 60%, and Dan Bin held on to the stock and added shares in the third quarter. Dongfang Harbor also increased its Nvidia holdings by nearly 150,000 shares in the third quarter, making the stock its second-largest holding.

data.title: Artemis Co-Founder Jon Ma Says Half His Net Worth Is in Anthropic and Plans to Sell BTC
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, Artemis co-founder Jon Ma said about half of his net worth is allocated to Anthropic, which he believes could become a leading AI company in cybersecurity, programming, law, healthcare, drug development and finance. He expects Anthropic to reach a $10 trillion market capitalization and said OpenAI could also benefit after going public.

Ma said he planned to sell all his other holdings that day, keep only ANT, GOOGL, META, NBIS and NVDA, and exit HOOD and BTC, citing what he sees as more attractive risk-reward in AI applications and the potential for compounding earnings and revenue. A portfolio screenshot he shared showed ANT at 52.1% and NVDA at 11.4%; FCNTX, VTSAX, NU, TSM, DDOG and GOOGL each accounted for less than 8%.

data.title: Moody's: UK Deficit Cuts Unlikely to Reverse Rising Debt Trend
data.description: According to Jin10, Moody's said the UK is reducing its fiscal deficit, but not enough to reverse the continued rise in government debt. Moody's expects the deficit-to-GDP ratio to fall from 5.3% in 2025 to 4.5% in 2026 and 4% in 2027. The UK government's 2027 budget also reflects its commitment to reducing the deficit. However, Moody's expects government debt to rise to 106% of GDP by the end of this decade, while interest rates are expected to remain high relative to government revenue. Moody's said the long average maturity of UK government debt and the country's mature domestic capital markets help limit refinancing and liquidity risks.

data.title: U.S. Agriculture Department Cyberattack Raises Food-Safety Information Concerns
data.description: According to Jin10, the U.S. Department of Agriculture was targeted in a cyberattack this week, raising concerns that sensitive food-safety information could be exposed. Two former department officials told NBC that the agency informed employees on Thursday that a system used to pay farmers had been attacked. The officials said the breach was limited to the payment database, but hackers might have been able to access sensitive food-safety information. The U.S. government is investigating, but has not identified those responsible. The attack is the latest in a series of technical disruptions and cyberattacks over the past week and more, including service interruptions at Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration, several banks, and the National Security Agency’s classified communications system. The Trump administration says the incidents are unrelated.

data.title: USDT Circulating Supply Falls 5.03 Billion in 20 Days as Tether Burns 8 Billion Unissued Tokens
data.description: Tether burned 8 billion unissued USDT, while the token’s circulating supply fell by a net 5.03 billion over 20 days. According to Odaily, Lookonchain reported that the burns comprised three Ethereum transactions: 2 billion USDT at 22:58 (UTC+8) on November 2, another 2 billion at 00:13 (UTC+8) on November 3, and 4 billion at 09:02 (UTC+8) on November 20. The tokens were unissued inventory held in Tether’s treasury; they were sent to a multisignature address before being burned and were not USDT held by users. Over the same period, circulating supply declined from about 179.8 billion on November 1 to about 174.77 billion on November 21.

data.title: Analyst: BTC Derivatives Liquidations Are Heavily Imbalanced as Yearlong Long Positions Near Clearance
data.description:
An analyst said BTC derivatives liquidations are heavily imbalanced, with most long positions accumulated over the past year nearly cleared. According to Odaily, crypto analyst Darkfost said in a post on X that total liquidations across the market exceeded $2.4 billion over the past 24 hours, with 92.5% coming from long positions. As the market continued to decline, most long positions accumulated over the past year were liquidated.

The liquidation heatmap showed about $1 billion in potential long liquidations near the current price, compared with as much as $23.5 billion in potential short liquidations above it.

data.title: Polymarket’s Ethereum 2026 Forecast: Below-$1,500 Odds Drop 15.95%
data.description: On Polymarket’s “Ethereum 2026 Price Prediction” market, the “Below $1,500” Yes option fell from 82.2% to 66.25%, a 15.95% drop over one hour. According to ChainCatcher, the odds were 82.2% one hour earlier.

data.title: Moody's: UK Growth Outperforms Expectations, but Inflation and Debt Risks Persist
data.description: According to Jin10, Moody's Ratings said the UK's economic growth in recent years has been stronger than expected, but risks remain. Improved relations with the European Union or stronger AI-related productivity growth could further boost medium-term economic growth, Moody's said. The UK still faces inflationary pressure and rising debt. Moody's said the country's economic outlook could weaken if the government struggles to cut its fiscal deficit, causing debt to grow faster.

data.title: Australia Says Gas Reservation Talks Continue Ahead of Expected Parliamentary Vote
data.description: According to Bloomberg, the Australian government said negotiations over its gas reservation proposals are continuing and it hopes the legislation will pass parliament in the coming week.

data.title: STOCKS | Tech Stocks Slide as AI Sentiment Cools, Nvidia Loses $2.7 Trillion in a Month and a Half
data.description:
AI investment sentiment weakened as technology shares sold off, and Nvidia lost about $2.7 trillion in market value in a month and a half. According to Odaily, major U.S. stock indexes plunged, while Nvidia fell 14.01% on the 20th to a 52-week low. Its market capitalization dropped to about $3 trillion, placing it fourth among U.S. stocks after Alphabet overtook it. Nvidia's market value has fallen from a record high of about $5.77 trillion set on the 6th of the previous month, a decline equivalent to Amazon's entire market capitalization.

Despite Nvidia's strong results and Anthropic's public listing, investor sentiment did not recover and the tech-led selloff continued. On its second day of trading, Anthropic gave back most of the previous day's gains and closed down 8.50%, after briefly falling near its $83 IPO price. Major financial media have mainly attributed Nvidia's decline to weakening AI investment sentiment, the broader tech selloff and concerns about the company's accounting.

data.title: Bitcoin Core Releases 30.5 and 31.3 to Fix AI-Discovered Vulnerability
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Bitcoin Core released versions 30.5 and 31.3 to fix a medium-severity vulnerability that could cause nodes to stall. The flaw was discovered by Loupe, an AI scanning tool from Spiral. The discontinued 29.x branch is not covered by the fix and will not receive a patch.

data.title: China Uses Summits to Expand Influence as Xi Hosts Trump and Putin
data.description: According to CNBC, Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin at a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday, after the leaders met at an APEC welcome banquet the previous evening. It was their first in-person meeting together. At the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting, Xi announced China would provide $20 million in support for the Asia Pacific region and advocated for an “Asia-Pacific community with a shared future.” Xi has hosted more than 40 heads of state so far this year, including at least eight around the APEC meetings in Shenzhen this week, after receiving over 60 state visits in 2025, according to official Chinese readouts. Tsinghua University researcher Jodie Wen said China’s engagement with major powers reflects its influence across the Global South and Eurasia, and that Beijing hopes to provide platforms for countries to discuss issues. EIU economist Yue Su said China uses multilateral platforms to expand its international influence and demonstrate its commitment to multilateralism, while focusing increasingly on economic benefits through trade, investment, financial connectivity and technology cooperation.

data.title: Analysts: Early Polar Vortex Breakdown Threatens Europe’s Depleted Gas Stocks
data.description: According to CNBC, an unprecedented early breakdown of the stratospheric polar vortex coinciding with a record-breaking El Niño has raised concerns about colder conditions and higher gas demand in Europe. European gas storage began the winter at its lowest level in more than a decade, and the International Energy Agency warned that low inventories and limited storage capacity in some importing countries could intensify competition for liquefied natural gas cargoes and put upward pressure on prices during periods of high demand. Wood Mackenzie gas analyst David Lewis said the combination of the early vortex breakdown and a strong El Niño has no historical precedent and could affect global gas demand. Rabobank senior energy strategist Florence Schmit warned that colder-than-expected weather could be difficult for Europe to manage, noting that gas storage withdrawals had been unusually strong over the previous two weeks. European gas prices reached 103.9 euros ($113.99) per megawatt hour in late October, their highest level since the 2022 energy crisis, while Dutch TTF futures for December delivery stood at around 87.28 euros on Friday afternoon.

data.title: Cyberattacks Expose Security Gaps at Europe’s Everyday Businesses
data.description: According to CNBC, attackers hit refrigeration systems in seven Swedish Coop stores in early November, after similar attacks on French supermarkets in October; Coop said security upgrades at the affected stores were scheduled for two days later and that the vulnerability has since been addressed. Sygnia handled 285% more incidents in October than a year earlier, CEO Guy Segal said, and some businesses seeking emergency assistance were turned away. Ahold Delhaize said a separate October cyberattack on its online operations and supply chain would reduce fourth-quarter sales by 200 million euros ($219 million).

data.title: Machi's Cumulative Papertrade Losses Reach $2.737 Million, Account Holds $4,411
data.description: Machi's cumulative losses on Papertrade have reached $2.737 million, with the account holding just $4,411 as of publication. According to Odaily, on-chain data show Machi recently moved to Papertrade but continued taking long positions in ETH, facing repeated liquidations during the latest market downturn. Machi transferred several thousand dollars into the account this morning and opened another highly leveraged ETH long during the midday market drop today.
